verdicts.summary: Decision call has no stale-session check. The CSRF token from the earlier details call is bound to a session id that can rotate, and the hosted consent page never reloads it. One approval can then fail until the page is reloaded.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The owner's hosted-app token for the environment is cached with about 1 min or more left. It is refreshed only inside the 60 s skew (service.ts:398). 2) /approve-agent loads. `approval` runs on session A and returns csrf=H(A, client, redirect, challenge) (McpOAuth.ts:310-319, 416). 3) The owner takes a minute to choose a level. The token crosses the skew, or the renewal loop at service.ts:576-597 renews it. Each exchange issues a new 1 h session (EnvironmentAuth.ts:978-986), so the id becomes B. 4) Approve calls `decision` with the renewed DPoP token on B and csrf(A). `approve` computes csrf(B) and rejects the mismatch (McpOAuth.ts:471-480). 5) `refused` is surfaced as 'Your session cannot approve this request. Enter a pairing code instead.' The hosted page has no code field. 6) McpConsent keeps the old `details` (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:201-221, 247). Every retry sends the same stale csrf on session B and fails again until the page is reloaded. The decision request sets no `isUnauthorizedResponse` (connectMcpApproval.ts:99-106), so nothing renews or reloads.
verdicts.consequence: A sign-in the owner is entitled to approve is refused. The message points to a code field that does not exist on this page, and retry cannot recover. The owner must reload /approve-agent, and the agent's authorize request may already be stale. It only hits when the token rotates mid-consent, which is rare.
verdicts.missing: On a CSRF-mismatch refusal the hosted transport should re-run `approval` to get a fresh csrfToken and retry once. Alternatively, rotate the token before showing consent.

verdicts.summary: The first authorization is bounded by the 30 s exchange timeout. The request plus one retry is bounded by 10 s. Every failure path maps to ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError.
verdicts.safe_line: packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/service.ts:445-454 caps the exchange at 30 s. packages/client-runtime/src/state/environmentHttpAuth.ts:260-271 wraps the whole loop in a 10 s timeoutOrElse.
verdicts.scenario: Tried a slow relay exchange at line 64, a retry exchange inside the loop, and a timeout while the exchange fork keeps running. No state is left behind: the fork is scoped (service.ts:465) and pendingTokens dedupes the next caller (service.ts:411-414). The result is a retryable 'Could not reach' error.

verdicts.summary: No caller omits `headers`, and the server reads credentials from the raw request, not from the parsed headers.
verdicts.safe_line: packages/contracts/src/environmentHttp.ts:92-95 and 655-669 make both fields optionalKey, so `headers: {}` is valid. A grep for `.approval(` and `.decision(` finds only ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:110/113, PeerLinks.ts:311 and connectMcpApproval.ts:93/104.
verdicts.scenario: Looked for a second caller, for a client that sends a cookie only, and for a DPoP request whose parsed header schema might drop `dpop`. `authenticateRequest` reads `request.headers` directly (EnvironmentAuth.ts:782-783). A cookie-only caller with `{}` takes the cookie path.

verdicts.summary: The only hazard I found in the automatic redirect is the dead end for visitors who are not the T3 Connect owner. That is the same issue as finding 0.
The flag is hard-coded true and read in one place. Whether the hosted app that serves /approve-agent at the configured URL has the new page depends on deploy order, which this checkout cannot show.
verdicts.missing: Deployment ordering between the server release and app.t3.codes / nightly.app.t3.codes. If the server ships first, the redirect at mcpOAuthHttp.ts:132 sends tunnel sign-ins to a host without the page. The wizard has already dropped its code, and the page's own beforeLoad redirects to '/'. Only the author or the release process can answer.

verdicts.summary: The client redirect gate accepts everything the server can register, including the bracketed IPv6 loopback.
verdicts.safe_line: apps/server/src/auth/McpOAuth.ts:109-112 allows only https, or http on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. packages/shared/src/preview.ts:52-56 accepts all of localhost, 127.0.0.1 and '[::1]' (WHATWG URL.hostname keeps the brackets).
verdicts.scenario: Tried http://[::1]:PORT/cb. It passes both checks. Tried a redirect URI with a custom scheme. The server refuses it at registration, so the client gate never sees it.

verdicts.summary: McpConsent's load and decide behave consistently for both transports. The one stale-state problem is the csrfToken issue in note 0.
verdicts.safe_line: apps/web/src/components/auth/ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:164-181 drops stale loads with the `cancelled` flag, and :208-221 always clears `pending` on a non-redirect answer.
verdicts.scenario: Tried a repeat load (StrictMode double mount), a redirect answer from load, and a failed decision. Repeat loads are independent because createRuntimeCommand defaults to parallel mode with a fresh atom per run (runtime.ts:435-446). A failed decision re-enables the buttons. A redirect from load that fails the URL check becomes 'invalid'.

verdicts.summary: The redirect gate matches the server's registration rule, so legitimate agent callbacks still pass.
verdicts.safe_line: apps/web/src/components/auth/ConnectAgentSurface.logic.ts:61-64 and apps/server/src/auth/McpOAuth.ts:109-112 enforce the same scheme and host set.
verdicts.scenario: Tried an http loopback callback with a port, an IPv6 loopback, and a javascript: or data: URL. The first two pass. The last is refused with a visible error and `pending` cleared (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:212-220).

verdicts.summary: The open question is answered. A hosted approval cannot be reached when the managed policy denies remote clients, and the runtime-mode ceiling is enforced at tool-call time, not at approval time. Dropping the wizard's Access gate hides no server-side refusal.
verdicts.safe_line: apps/server/src/policy/managedLimits.ts:76-77 makes allowsConnect require allowsRemoteClients. apps/server/src/cloud/CloudLink.ts:1627-1630 unlinks T3 Connect when it is false, so `state.linked` fails at mcpOAuthHttp.ts:81 and there is no hosted redirect.
verdicts.scenario: Tried a managed policy with `clients` lacking remote, and a policy rolled out after the link was made. In the first case T3 Connect cannot link. In the second it is unlinked at start, and cloud-connect sessions are revoked (EnvironmentAuth.ts:1443-1447). The runtime-mode ceiling is applied on every MCP call (McpHttpServer.ts:201, 235), so approving a higher level cannot exceed it. The consent page also disables above-ceiling options (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:396-403). The wizard no longer checks the device's Manage access permission. That only exposes the tunnel URL, because approval still needs the owner's own Connect session.

verdicts.summary: The wrapper matches its sibling and maps failures the same way. The relay session carries the scopes `approvingSession` needs, which answers finding 1's question.
verdicts.safe_line: apps/server/src/cloud/CloudLink.ts:1586-1588 mints the cloud-connect credential with AuthStandardClientScopes. That list includes access:write and orchestration:read (packages/contracts/src/auth.ts:150-167).
verdicts.scenario: Tried an owner session missing a scope. The relay mint always grants the full standard set, and the exchange can only narrow it if the client asks to (EnvironmentAuth.ts:971-974). The client requests no scopes (service.ts:297 is for the relay token, not the environment exchange). The csrf-less case therefore means a stale or invalid credential, not missing scopes. It also cannot be an MCP-client token, because `rejectMcpClientAudience` blocks it (EnvironmentAuth.ts:745).
